result.title: LEDGE: Separating Critic and Editor Failures in Text-to-Image Self-Correction
result.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) self-correction combines a vision-language model (VLM) critic that diagnoses errors and proposes instructions with an image editor that executes them. End-to-end evaluation obscures whether failures arise from incorrect diagnoses or an editor unable to execute valid instructions. We introduce LEDGE (Learning Error Diagnosis in Generation and Editing), a framework that separates these bottlenecks. LEDGE compiles oracle edit instructions from GenEval while holding the generated images and the editor fixed, isolating the editor's correction capability from the critic's diagnostic accuracy. On Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, oracle instructions raise GenEval from 72.0% to 81.2%, versus 74.1% for the baseline VLM critic. Yet 435 of 644 failed images remain unrepaired, exposing a substantial editor gap. We also use oracle labels from disjoint training prompts to supervise the critic. Oracle supervision raises exact diagnosis from 33.3% (the same VLM with our structured output, untrained) to 70.8%. With the same editor, the resulting critic improves GenEval from 42.2% (uncorrected) to 59.4% on Stable Diffusion 1.5, against 50.9% for the baseline critic, and from 72.0% to 76.0% on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, despite training only on Stable Diffusion 1.5. Improvements transfer to unseen object classes, a second editor, and independent T2I-CompBench judges and prompts. A small human evaluation confirms the ranking in estimated net corrections but suggests a smaller gain than detector-based evaluation. LEDGE thus distinguishes two limits of self-correction: knowing what to fix and being able to fix it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LEDGE 框架，用 GenEval 编译的 oracle 编辑指令固定图像与编辑器，把 text-to-image 自纠正的失败拆成「VLM 评论者诊断错误」与「编辑器无法执行」两类，并用 oracle 标签监督评论者的结构化诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把诊断与执行解耦、以 oracle 标签监督 VLM 评论者的思路，可能为 LVR 中推理状态与答案生成的贡献分配、视觉证据筛选质量的评估提供可核查线索，但研究对象是图像编辑流程而非 latent 推理状态。
